findings.title: Portable Run address gate has no physical path-component length bound
findings.problem: 025 closes the Win32 reserved-device-name gap, but the Explore candidate gate still accepts arbitrarily long lowercase ASCII segments because its grammar/basename/normalize/reserved-name checks define no length limit. A 256-character segment passes that gate and both POSIX/Win32 lexical checks, yet the detached Linux filesystem reports NAME_MAX=255 and rejects creation with ENAMETOOLONG. Windows documentation likewise bounds individual NTFS/exFAT path components at 255 characters. Therefore the current proof still does not establish the claimed portable canonical repository segment.
reviewEvidence: 025 ZIP SHA-256 matches its supplied checksum.
RE-024-001 reserved-device class is independently reproduced as rejected while canonical dated Action segments remain accepted.
A 255-character lowercase ASCII segment passes the documented gate and can be created on the detached Linux filesystem.
A 256-character lowercase ASCII segment also passes the documented gate, path.posix/path.win32 basename and normalize checks, but actual directory creation fails with ENAMETOOLONG.
getconf NAME_MAX for the detached filesystem reports 255.
Microsoft documents individual NTFS/exFAT file-name/path-component limits of 255 characters.
requiredRevision: Extend R7 / repository-address contract to include physical path-component length as a portability risk.
Define an explicit bounded canonical physical segment before filesystem use: at most 255 ASCII characters under the current proof grammar, or a stricter project-defined cap.

Add boundary proof demonstrating the maximum accepted length and rejection immediately beyond the bound, while preserving the previous traversal/separator/absolute/drive/UNC/alias/reserved-device negatives.

State explicitly that total repository path length / checkout-root constraints are environment or later Windows acceptance concerns if they are not being claimed by this Change; do not silently treat lexical containment as proof of total-path portability.
Keep final logical Run occurrence identity/display format and sequence allocation open.
nonRequirements: No production implementation is required in revise-explore.
No final logical RunId display/string schema must be frozen.
No Windows whole-manager Full Test is required at this boundary.
No symlink/junction/reparse-point hardening is added by this finding.
No Result admission, Policy, scheduler, database/WAL, or multi-Agent recovery work is required.
